### Backend & Architecture
- **Languages**: Java, TypeScript / JavaScript, Rust, Go, Python
- **Frameworks**: Spring Boot, Spring Security, NestJS, Axum, FastAPI
- **Authentication & Security**: Dual-token JWT (short-lived access tokens paired with HttpOnly/SameSite refresh cookies), RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), Argon2 / BCrypt hashing, XSS/CSRF mitigation
- **Protocols & Communication**: RESTful APIs, Server-Sent Events (SSE), WebSockets, HTTP/2, mDNS zero-configuration discovery

### Mobile & Desktop
- **Android**: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Android Architecture Components, Hilt (Dependency Injection), Coroutines & Flow, Rust FFI
- **Desktop**: Rust, Tauri v2, Svelte 5, MSIX packaging, SignPath Foundation Windows binary signing, Microsoft Store publishing

### Databases, Storage & Caching
- **Relational Databases**: PostgreSQL, SQLite
- **ORMs & Query Builders**: Drizzle ORM, Spring Data JPA / Hibernate
- **Caching & In-Memory**: LRU byte-budget in-memory caching
- **Vector Search**: Qdrant, BM25 hybrid retrieval

### Networking & P2P
- **Protocols**: iroh (QUIC-based local-first P2P with automatic NAT traversal and hole-punching), Axum embedded HTTP local servers, mDNS

### Infrastructure, DevOps & Cloud
- **Containers**: Docker, Docker Compose, multi-stage lightweight builds
- **OS & Hosting**: Linux (Debian, Ubuntu), VPS administration, Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare Pages, Wrangler CLI
- **CI/CD & Version Control**: Git, GitHub Actions, semantic release automation
- **AI & Computer Vision**: Claude Code, OpenAI API, Ollama (local LLM inference), manga-ocr, OpenCV

## Featured Projects

### 1. Acerola Android
- **Status**: Pre-release
- **Category**: Native Mobile App (Android)
- **Description**: Native Android manga and comic reader built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. Scans local storage, parses CBZ/CBR archives, and automatically fetches rich metadata from MangaDex and AniList.
- **Key Architectural Highlights**:
  - *Storage Scanner*: Traverses and indexes designated external/internal storage directories to compile a comprehensive local library without manual rescanning.
  - *Metadata Fetcher*: Enriches local titles with high-resolution covers, synopses, authors, genres, and chapter indexes by querying MangaDex API, AniList API, and parsing embedded ComicInfo.xml metadata.
  - *Archive & Format Processing*: Native decompressor for CBZ (ZIP) and CBR (RAR) comic archives with zero-temp-file stream extraction; automated on-demand PDF conversion on first launch.
  - *High-performance Reader Engine*: Flexible reading surface supporting horizontal paginated, vertical paginated, and seamless infinite webtoon scroll modes with automatic progress persistence down to the exact page.
- **Tech Stack**: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Rust, Iroh, Hilt, MangaDex API, AniList API
- **Links**:
  - [Acerola Android GitHub](https://github.com/vinicius-gpl/acerola-reader/tree/main/acerola/android)
  - [Acerola Monorepo GitHub](https://github.com/vinicius-gpl/acerola-reader)
  - [Acerola Reader Documentation](https://docs.acerola.app/)

### 2. Acerola Desktop
- **Status**: In Development / Officially Published on Microsoft Store
- **Category**: Cross-Platform Desktop Application
- **Description**: Modern comic and manga reader for desktop built with Rust and Tauri v2 with a responsive Svelte 5 frontend. Reads CBZ, CBR, and PDF files, organizes local collections, streams pages over local HTTP via Axum to companion mobile devices, and connects to AI translation plugins.
- **Key Architectural Highlights**:
  - *Native Rust Reader Engine*: High-speed extraction of CBZ, CBR, and PDF pages powered by Rust with an LRU byte-budget memory cache, ensuring instantaneous page flips without stutter or disk churn.
  - *Embedded Mobile Server*: Spawns a lightweight local Axum HTTP server so the companion Android app can browse and stream the user's PC library over local Wi-Fi without transferring files.
  - *AI Translation Plugin Integration*: Seamless integration with Acerola Translator; uploads CBZ archives and tracks real-time progress via Server-Sent Events (SSE), downloading the translated comic automatically once rendered.
  - *Zero-Config mDNS Discovery*: Automatically detects instances of Acerola Android and Acerola Translator across the local network without IP configuration.
  - *Code Signing & Microsoft Store*: Windows binaries signed via SignPath Foundation for open-source GPL3 compliance and officially published on the Microsoft Store.
- **Tech Stack**: Rust, Tauri v2, Svelte 5, TypeScript, Iroh, Tailwind, Axum
- **Links**:
  - [Acerola Desktop GitHub](https://github.com/vinicius-gpl/acerola-reader/tree/main/acerola/desktop)
  - [Acerola Monorepo GitHub](https://github.com/vinicius-gpl/acerola-reader)
  - [Acerola Reader Documentation](https://docs.acerola.app/)
  - [Preview Banner Image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vinicius-gpl/acerola-reader/main/docs/github/ptbr/desktop/banner/acerola-desktop-solo.png)
  - [Screenshot - Home Screen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vinicius-gpl/acerola-reader/main/docs/github/ptbr/desktop/prints/home-screen.png)

### 3. Brand Maker
- **Status**: Shipped / Live
- **Category**: Brand Identity & AI-Agent Design System Tooling
- **Description**: Static web app that builds a brand's visual identity on screen with a live preview and downloads a design kit that keeps the AI coding agent (Claude Code) on the standard: skills, hooks and dependency-free `.mjs` checkers, plus design tokens in CSS and Tailwind v4.
- **Key Architectural Highlights**:
  - *Palettes, Patterns and Finishes*: 30 palettes in 7 groups, 10 interface patterns (Simple, Material 3 Expressive, Fluent 2, Carbon, Primer, shadcn, Cupertino, GOV.UK, Brutalist, Blueprint) and 7 finishes, applied live to a sample site in light and dark modes.
  - *Design Rules*: No pure black or white, WCAG AA contrast computed live for every text/background pair, and the 7 UX laws with adjustable limits.
  - *Agent Design Kit*: The zip ships Claude Code skills, hooks and `.mjs` scripts (with `node --test` tests) that check every edited file against the brand.
  - *100% Static*: The kit is generated in the browser — nothing leaves the user's machine. Deployed to GitHub Pages on a custom domain, with a Caddy Docker image as an alternative.
- **Tech Stack**: SvelteKit, Svelte 5, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, Vitest, Docker, GitHub Pages
- **Links**:
  - [Brand Maker (live)](https://brand-maker.vinicius-gpl.com)
  - [Brand Maker GitHub](https://github.com/vinicius-gpl/brand-maker)
  - [Preview Banner Image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vinicius-gpl/brand-maker/main/docs/banner/banner.jpg)

### 4. Acerola Ticket
- **Status**: Shipped / Done
- **Category**: IT Service Desk & Systems Management Platform
- **Description**: Comprehensive IT asset management and service desk platform featuring support tickets, hardware inventory, preventive maintenance tracking, and a systems Kanban integrated with GitHub. Includes an automated Go Windows monitoring agent.
- **Key Architectural Highlights**:
  - *Support Ticket System*: Employees submit and track support tickets with attachments and screenshots; ticket access, prioritization, and assignment are governed by granular module permissions.
  - *Hardware Inventory & Maintenance*: Tracks corporate computers, replacement parts, scheduled preventive maintenance cycles, and machine disposal histories with per-device audit trails.
  - *GitHub Integration & Systems Kanban*: Synchronizes merged pull requests, closed GitHub issues, and release milestones into an interactive Kanban board and chronological delivery schedule.
  - *Go Windows Background Agent*: Standalone Go service installed on workstation machines that captures hardware metrics and automatically updates itself to published LTS versions.
- **Tech Stack**: TypeScript, SvelteKit, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Go, Docker
- **Links**:

### 5. Acerola Translator
- **Status**: Future Idea / Architecture Defined
- **Category**: Computer Vision & AI Translation Service
- **Description**: Automated manga and webtoon translation pipeline that detects speech balloons, runs Japanese OCR, translates dialogue using modern LLMs, cleans the original text with inpainting, and typesets translated Portuguese text.
- **Key Architectural Highlights**:
  - *End-to-End Vision Pipeline*: Multi-stage job processing each comic page through contour/speech balloon detection → OCR → LLM translation → background inpainting → typography re-render.
  - *Parallel Asynchronous Ingestion*: Multiple pages processed concurrently with real-time SSE progress streaming to connected clients.
  - *Multi-Provider LLM Integration*: Unified interface abstracting Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, and local Ollama instances for offline or private translation workflows.
  - *Hybrid Polyglot Runtime*: Go orchestrator handling HTTP requests, job queues, and SSE, alongside a persistent Python worker running manga-ocr in GPU/CPU memory to eliminate warm-up latency.
  - *Single-Command Deployment*: Packaged as a turnkey multi-container Docker Compose stack.
- **Tech Stack**: Go, Python, FastAPI, OpenCV, manga-ocr, Svelte 5, Docker

### 6. Acerola Relay
- **Status**: Future Idea / Architecture Defined
- **Category**: P2P Synchronization & Relay Infrastructure
- **Description**: Peer-to-peer sync and relay server bridging the desktop client, mobile reader, and translator in the Acerola ecosystem, ensuring libraries, reading progress, and translated files stay synchronized across devices without a central cloud database.
- **Key Architectural Highlights**:
  - *Decentralized P2P with iroh*: Built on top of the iroh QUIC protocol for direct peer-to-peer connectivity, penetrating corporate NATs and router firewalls without manual port forwarding.
  - *Secure Zero-Config Remote Access*: Exposes local comic libraries securely to mobile devices away from home without VPN setup.
  - *Multi-Device State Consistency*: Synchronizes reading progress, bookmarks, and translated files between Android and desktop automatically.
  - *Lightweight Self-Hosting*: Minimal memory footprint packaged as a standalone Docker container suitable for Raspberry Pi, home labs, or budget VPS instances.
- **Tech Stack**: Rust, iroh (QUIC), SQLite, Docker
